newsitem.title: USA: Weaker aluminum prices mask rising demand - Spector.
newsitem.headline: Weaker aluminum prices mask rising demand - Spector.

text.p: There appears to be a disconnect between market sentiment and the accumulating evidence that destocking is over and physical demand for aluminum is on the rise, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.

"Part of the problem, especially when it comes to sentiment, is the time lag between the availability of industry data, and the time it takes the market players to digest and interpret the statistics," Spector writes in his Aluminum Service Industry newsletter.
Despite sluggish aluminum prices, trends included Western world primary ingot shipments rising by three percent in July this year compared to the same month in 1995, according to preliminary data.
Brazilian shipments could rise 10.9 percent this year from last year's level, according to domestic industry association ABAL.

The U.S., the world's biggest aluminum consumer, is seeing a "sharp pick up in demand", Spector said. And through September 20, orders in the last three months were up 20 to 26 percent on last year. Orders lead shipments by one month, Spector noted.
There are also signs of a pick up in Europe and Japan coming out of the doldrums.
"As we move into the fourth quarter, it is not difficult to see how LME stocks could start to decline," Spector said.
